questions.question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 76 and the third number is 107. Find the average of the remaining two numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of five numbers = 655

The average of the first two numbers = 76

The third number = 107

**Formula used:**

Sum of first two numbers = Average × Number of terms

Sum of remaining two numbers = Total sum - (Sum of first two numbers + Third number)

Average = Sum

questions.question: Kanchan bought 52 books for Rs 1130 each from one shop and 47 books for Rs 905 each from another. What is the average price (in Rs) he paid per book ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

52 books at ₹1130 each

47 books at ₹905 each

**Formula used:**

Average price = Total cost ÷ Total number of books

**Calculation:**

Total cost = (52 × 1130) + (47 × 905)

⇒ 58760 + 42535 = 101295

Total books = 52 + 47 = 99

Average price = 101295 ÷ 99

⇒ Average price = ₹1023.18

**∴ The average price per book is ₹1023.18.**

questions.question: The average of the marks of 14 students in a class is 63. If the marks of each student are doubled, find the new average?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of marks = 63

Number of students = 14

**Formula used:**

New Average = Old Average × Multiplier

**Calculation:**

Old Total Marks = Average × Number of Students

⇒ Old Total Marks = 63 × 14

⇒ Old Total Marks = 882

When marks are doubled, New Total Marks = 882 × 2

⇒ New Total Marks = 1764

New Average = New Total Marks ÷ Number of Students

⇒ New Average = 1764 ÷ 14

⇒ New Average = 126

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: The average age of 10 members of a family is 34 years. If the youngest member is 7 years old, what was the average age (in years) of the family members just before the birth of the youngest member?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Current family members = 10

Current average age = 34 years

Youngest member's age = 7 years

**Calculations:**

Current total age = 10 × 34 = 340 years

Before youngest's birth (7 years ago):

Number of members = 10 - 1 = 9

Total age reduction due to time passing = 10 members × 7 years = 70 years

Total age of 9 members 7 years ago = 340 - 70 = 270 years

Average age 7 years ago = 270 / 9 = 30 years

**∴ The average age was 30 years.**

questions.question: The average weight of a class of 82 students is 62.5 kg. If the average weight of half of the students is 83.6 kg, then find the average weight (in kg) of the remaining students of the class.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of students in the class = 82

Average weight of the class = 62.5 kg

Average weight of half of the students (41 students) = 83.6 kg

**Formula used:**

Total weight of students = Number of students × Average weight

Remaining students' average weight = (Total weight of students - Weight of first half) ÷ Number of remaining students

**Calculation:**

Total weight of the class = 82 × 62.5

⇒ Total weight = 5125 kg

Weight of first half of students = 41 × 83.6

⇒ Weight of first half = 3427.6 kg

Weight of remaining students = Total weight - Weight of first half

⇒ Weight of remaining students = 5125 - 3427.6

⇒ Weight of remaining students = 1697.4 kg

Average weight of remaining students = Weight of remaining students ÷ Number of remaining students

⇒ Average weight = 1697.4 ÷ 41

⇒ Average weight = 41.4 kg

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: In an exam, the average marks obtained by John in English, Maths, Hindi and Drawing were 50.5. His average marks in Maths, Science, Social Studies and Craft were 70. If the average marks in all seven subjects was 58, his score in Maths was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average marks in English, Maths, Hindi, Drawing = 50.5

Average marks in Maths, Science, Social Studies, Craft = 70

Average marks in all seven subjects = 58

**Formula Used:**

Average = dfrac{{Sum of scores}}{{Number of subjects}}

**Calculation:**

Sum of scores (English + Maths + Hindi + Drawing) = 50.5 × 4 = 202

Sum of scores (Maths + Science + Social Studies + Craft) = 70 × 4 = 280

Let M = Maths score, E = English score, H = Hindi score, D = Drawing score, S = Science score, SS = Social Studies score, C = Craft score

E + M + H + D = 202 ---(1)

M + S + SS + C = 280 ---(2)

Total sum of scores in 7 subjects = E + M + H + D + S + SS + C = 58 × 7 = 406

From (1) and (2):

(E + M + H + D) + (M + S + SS + C) = 202 + 280

E + 2M + H + D + S + SS + C = 482

We know (E + M + H + D + S + SS + C) + M = 482

406 + M = 482

⇒ M = 482 - 406 = 76

**∴ His score in Maths was 76.**

questions.question: The average of the first 25 multiples of 3 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The average of any **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** is given by: (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2

First multiple of 3 = 3 × 1 = 3

25th multiple of 3 = 3 × 25 = 75

Average = (3 + 75) ÷ 2 = 78 ÷ 2 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The number of terms (n) = 25 and the base number (x) = 3.

**Formula Used:** Average of first **n** multiples of **x** = x × (n + 1) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48bc8a595afb44da003443801102aa01618ceb3b87aee865b85528c0faf600d9.png] 

⇒ First multiple = 3 × 1 = 3

⇒ Last multiple = 3 × 25 = 75

⇒ Average = (3 + 75) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 78 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is calculated using the formula: Sₙ = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of AP

For any sequence in **Arithmetic Progression**, the average is always the middle term (if n is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if n is even).

Sum of Multiples

The sum of the first n multiples of x is x × [n(n + 1) ÷ 2]. Dividing this by n gives the average formula: x × (n + 1) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: The average height of 50 pupils in a class is 150 cm. Five of them whose average height is 146 cm, leave the class, and five others whose average height is 156 cm, join. The new average height of the pupils of the class (in cm) is _________.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net change in total height = **Number of pupils replaced** × (**Average of Joiners** − **Average of Leavers**)

Net change = 5 × (156 − 146) = 5 × 10 = +50 cm.

Increase in class average = Net change ÷ **Total pupils** = 50 ÷ 50 = +1 cm.

New average height = **Old average** + **Increase** = 150 + 1 = 151 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 151 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Average Height** = 150 cm, **Total Pupils** = 50.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b3ffdbae81cd83310d9a47caf262307a2cdb1b53337af4971b08fd6dcf67eff.png] 
⇒ **Total initial height** = 50 × 150 = 7500 cm.
⇒ Total height of 5 pupils who **left** = 5 × 146 = 730 cm.
⇒ Total height of 5 pupils who **joined** = 5 × 156 = 780 cm.
⇒ **New total height** of the class = 7500 − 730 + 780 = 7550 cm.
⇒ **New average height** = 7550 ÷ 50 = 151 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 151 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations). To find the new sum, add the value of joining members and subtract the value of leaving members.

Replacement Rule

When the number of people remains the same, the New Average = Old Average + (Net Change in Values ÷ Total Number). This is the fastest way to solve exchange-based problems.

Weighted Average

For two groups, Average = (n₁×A₁ + n₂×A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and A is the individual average.</p

questions.question: The average of all the prime numbers between 30 and 50 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

List all **prime numbers** between 30 and 50: 31, 37, 41, 43, 47.

Total count of prime numbers (n) = 5.

Sum of these primes = 31 + 37 + 41 + 43 + 47 = 199.

Average = Sum ÷ n = 199 ÷ 5 = 39.8.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The range of numbers is between **30** and **50**.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bdb0fce88c65dfab341ead1725304fb7a7dbc6ab69f3a85602ea803155447990.png] 

⇒ Identify **Prime Numbers** between 30 and 50: 31, 37, 41, 43, and 47.

⇒ Count of these numbers (n) = 5

⇒ **Sum** = 31 + 37 + 41 + 43 + 47

⇒ **Sum** = 199

⇒ **Average** = 199 ÷ 5

⇒ **Average** = 39.8

**∴ The correct answer is 39.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers Definition

A **prime number** is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

Even Prime Number

The number **2** is the only **even prime number**. All other prime numbers are odd numbers.

Sum of First N Primes

There is no simple polynomial formula for the sum of the first **n** prime numbers, so they must be listed and summed individually.

Average of a Set

The arithmetic mean or **average** of a set is always greater than the smallest number and less than the largest number in the set.</p

questions.question: The average monthly salary of a person for the months of January, February, March and April is ₹8,000 and that for the months of February, March, April and May is ₹8,500. If his salary for the month of May is ₹6,500, find his salary for the month of January.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Totals** = Number of Months × Difference in **Average**

⇒ May − January = 4 × (8,500 − 8,000) = 4 × 500 = ₹2,000

⇒ 6,500 − January = 2,000

⇒ January = 6,500 − 2,000 = ₹4,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4500.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average salary (Jan + Feb + Mar + Apr) = ₹8,000

Average salary (Feb + Mar + Apr + May) = ₹8,500

Salary for the month of **May** = ₹6,500

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c7507f558a91f8090c6de626c7711fa505d98f8d55039e553d5f06e705f6079.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total salary (Jan + Feb + Mar + Apr) = 8,000 × 4 = ₹32,000 --- (1)

⇒ Total salary (Feb + Mar + Apr + May) = 8,500 × 4 = ₹34,000 --- (2)

⇒ Subtracting equation (1) from equation (2):

⇒ (Feb + Mar + Apr + May) − (Jan + Feb + Mar + Apr) = 34,000 − 32,000

⇒ May − Jan = 2,000

⇒ 6,500 − Jan = 2,000

⇒ Jan = 6,500 − 2,000

⇒ Jan = ₹4,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4500.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Formula

The **Average** of a set of data is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations.

Replacement Property

When one value in a group is **replaced** by another, the change in the total is given by: (New Value − Old Value) = Number of items × Change in Average.

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the individual average.

questions.question: The average of the first 30 natural numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **average** of the first **n natural numbers** is always given by the formula: **(n + 1) ÷ 2**.

Here, the number of terms **n = 30**.

Average = (30 + 1) ÷ 2

Average = 31 ÷ 2 = 15.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First 30 natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, ..., 30.

**Formula Used:** Sum of first n natural numbers = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2 and Average = Sum ÷ n.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e7d42e33564c4361ae44eada1faf2a232d32fcb9268276694cf3642e8a336ad.png] 

⇒ Total numbers (n) = 30

⇒ Sum = [30 × (30 + 1)] ÷ 2

⇒ Sum = 15 × 31 = 465

⇒ Average = 465 ÷ 30

⇒ Average = 15.5

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The total sum is calculated as S = [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any Arithmetic Progression, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of Squares and Cubes

Sum of squares = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6 | Sum of cubes = [[n(n + 1)] ÷ 2]².

Average of First n Even/Odd Numbers

Average of first n even numbers = n + 1 | Average of first n odd numbers = n.</p

questions.question: The average of 10 observations is 46. It was realised later that an observation was misread as 42 in place of 142. Find the correct average.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net change in **Sum** = **Correct value** − **Incorrect value** = 142 − 42 = 100

Net change in **Average** = **Net change in Sum** ÷ **Total observations** = 100 ÷ 10 = 10

**Correct Average** = **Initial Average** + **Increase** = 46 + 10 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of **observations** (n) = 10

Incorrect **average** = 46

Incorrect **value** = 42

Correct **value** = 142

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/878534ede6cdde197fe982534a556ff4ed36c0f21c7af8a3968a9b0f4b794c25.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Incorrect Total Sum = 10 × 46 = 460

⇒ Correct Total Sum = Incorrect Sum − Incorrect Value + Correct Value

⇒ Correct Total Sum = 460 − 42 + 142

⇒ Correct Total Sum = 460 + 100 = 560

⇒ Correct Average = 560 ÷ 10 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The average represents the central value of a data set. If one value is replaced, the change in average is equal to the net difference divided by the total count.

Weighted Average

When two groups with different averages are combined, the combined average is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Successive Changes in Average

If every number in a set is increased by a constant **k**, the average of the set also increases by **k**.</p

questions.question: The average of the first twelve multiples of 11 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Average of first **n multiples** of **k** = k × (n + 1) / 2

Here, k = 11 and n = 12.

Average = 11 × (12 + 1) / 2 = 11 × 13 / 2

Average = 143 / 2 = 71.5

**∴ The correct answer is 71.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First twelve **multiples** of 11 are 11, 22, 33, ..., 132.

**Formula Used:** Average of an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** = (First term + Last term) / 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61c807dfcb7f5ef4b25232a06589372163d04a868b0b13bcd02175721694a348.png] 

⇒ First term (a) = 11 × 1 = 11

⇒ Last term (l) = 11 × 12 = 132

⇒ Total terms (n) = 12

⇒ Average = (11 + 132) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 143 ÷ 2 = 71.5

**∴ The correct answer is 71.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence of numbers where the difference between consecutive terms is constant. Multiples of any number always form an **AP**.

Sum of n terms in AP

The sum is calculated as Sₙ = (n/2) × (a + l), where a is the first term and l is the last term.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any set of **consecutive numbers** or terms in AP, the average is always the mean of the first and last terms.</p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7651214cf815f87a1f989fe8d376bb956c6dc40ad8c41522257d55b7d71ae724.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Sum = 30 + 19 + 23 + 29

⇒ Sum = 101

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Prime Number

A **prime number** is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

Properties of Averages

If each number in a set is increased by a constant 'k', the **average** also increases by 'k'.

First 10 Prime Numbers

questions.question: The average of 70 values is 40. If each value is multiplied by 20, what will be the changed average?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If each value in a data set is **multiplied** by a constant **k**, the **average** of the set is also multiplied by **k**.

Here, the **Initial Average** is **40** and each value is multiplied by **20**.

**New Average** = **Initial Average** × 20

**New Average** = 40 × 20 = 800.

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of values (n) = **70**

Average of these values = **40**

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all values) ÷ (Total number of values)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4fd1d9cf3afdfe7a542885642b8144b5d739c9c513e6f4fb0af043d7f674d056.png] 

⇒ Sum of **70 values** = Average × n

⇒ **Initial Sum** = 40 × 70 = 2800

⇒ If each value is multiplied by **20**, the **New Sum** = (x₁ × 20) + (x₂ × 20) + ... + (x₇₀ × 20)

⇒ **New Sum** = 20 × (x₁ + x₂ + ... + x₇₀) = 20 × 2800 = 56000

⇒ **New Average** = New Sum ÷ 70

⇒ **New Average** = 56000 ÷ 70 = 800

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

**__Additional Information__**

Addition and Subtraction Rule

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every value in a set, the new average will be (Old Average + **k**) or (Old Average − **k**) respectively.

Division Rule

If every value in a set is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the new average will be (Old Average ÷ **k**).

Combined Average

The average of two groups with n₁ and n₂ elements and averages A₁ and A₂ is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The sum of five consecutive numbers is 260. The sum of the first and the last numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a set of **consecutive numbers**, the **Average** is always the middle term.

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of terms = 260 ÷ 5 = 52

For any set of numbers in **Arithmetic Progression**, the sum of the 1st and last terms is equal to twice the average.

Sum of first and last = 2 × Average = 2 × 52 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of 5 consecutive numbers = 260.

**Formula Used:** Let the five **consecutive numbers** be x, (x + 1), (x + 2), (x + 3), and (x + 4).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d648d40f5f810e52f613e0c7515e2f59a5dd8fe882fd3f59d58ff823ded8834.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) + (x + 4) = 260

⇒ 5x + 10 = 260

⇒ 5x = 260 − 10

⇒ 5x = 250

⇒ x = 50

⇒ First number = x = 50

⇒ Last number = x + 4 = 50 + 4 = 54

⇒ Sum of first and last numbers = 50 + 54 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

Consecutive numbers form an **Arithmetic Progression** with a common difference of 1. The sum of such a series is given by S = n ÷ 2 × (a + l), where a is the first term and l is the last term.

Middle Term Property

For an odd number of terms (n), the **Average** is exactly equal to the middle term. For a set of 5 numbers, the 3rd number is the average.

Equidistant Sum Rule

In any AP, the sum of terms **equidistant** from the beginning and the end is constant. Thus, First + Last = Second + Second Last = 2 × Middle term.</p

questions.question: A group of people consists of men, women, and children. 40% of them are men, 35% are women and rest are children, and their average weights are 70 kg, 60 kg and 30 kg, respectively. The average weight of the group is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the total **group** size is 100 people.

Total Weight = (40 × 70) + (35 × 60) + (25 × 30)

Total Weight = 2800 + 2100 + 750 = 5650 kg

**Average weight** = 5650 ÷ 100 = 56.5 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of **Men** = 40%, **Average weight** = 70 kg

Percentage of **Women** = 35%, **Average weight** = 60 kg

Percentage of **Children** = Rest, **Average weight** = 30 kg

Weighted Average Formula

The average of a group consisting of multiple sub-groups is given by: Average = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂ + ... + nₖwₖ) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ... + nₖ), where n is the quantity and w is the weight/value.

Deviation Method for Averages

You can assume a base average (e.g., 50) and calculate the net deviation from this base for each part of the group to find the final average quickly.

Percentage Representation

When parts of a whole are given in percentages, the sum must always equal 100%. This is useful to find any missing component.</p

questions.question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 80, and that of the rest is 75. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **students** = 12 : (30 − 12) = 12 : 18 = **2 : 3**.

Using **deviation method**: Assume base average = 75.

Extra points from 2 parts = 2 × (80 − 75) = **+10**.

Net increase in average = 10 ÷ (2 + 3) = **2**.

Final **average score** = 75 + 2 = 77.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **students** = 30

Number of **Group 1** students = 12, Average = 80

Number of **Group 2** students = 30 − 12 = 18, Average = 75

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7f2fb34f8d0266ad360fefb7a191c5a710025ac6a007543f5790e134bbc4bb7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of scores of 12 students = 12 × 80 = 960

⇒ Sum of scores of remaining 18 students = 18 × 75 = 1350

⇒ Total sum of scores for 30 students = 960 + 1350 = 2310

⇒ Average score of the class = 2310 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score = 77

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two or more groups are combined, the combined average is calculated as Aw = Σ(nᵢ × aᵢ) ÷ Σnᵢ, where n is the number of items and a is the average.

Properties of Average

If every value in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the average also increases or decreases by **k**.

Combined Average with Ratio

If the number of elements in two groups are in ratio **x : y**, the combined average depends only on this ratio, not the absolute number of elements.</p

questions.question: The weights (in kg) of 9 members of a school cricket team are 50, 63, x, 62, 64, 48, 51, 55, 48. If the mean weight is 56 kg, then the value of x is ________.

Known deviations from 56: (50−56), (63−56), (62−56), (64−56), (48−56), (51−56), (55−56), (48−56)

⇒ −6, +7, +6, +8, −8, −5, −1, −8

Sum of known deviations = −7

For the total deviation to be zero, the deviation of **x** must be +7.

x = Mean + 7 = 56 + 7 = 63.

**∴ The correct answer is 63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

**Calculations:**

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The sum of the **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero: Σ(xᵢ − Mean) = 0.

Effect of Changes

If every observation is **increased** or **decreased** by a constant k, the mean is also increased or decreased by k.

Combined Mean

If two groups have means M₁ and M₂ with sizes n₁ and n₂, the **combined mean** is (n₁M₁ + n₂M₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: Nirmal bought 52 books from one shop for Rs 1130 each and 47 books from another for Rs. 900 each. What is the average price (in Rs) he paid per book ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume a base **average price** of 1000.

Deviation for 52 books at 1130 = 52 × (+130) = +6760

Deviation for 47 books at 900 = 47 × (−100) = −4700

Net deviation = 6760 − 4700 = 2060

Average deviation = 2060 ÷ (52 + 47) = 2060 ÷ 99 ≈ 20.81

Actual Average = 1000 + 20.81 = 1020.81

**∴ The correct answer is 1020.81.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of **books** from Shop 1 = 52, Price = 1130 each

Quantity of **books** from Shop 2 = 47, Price = 900 each

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16f248f219e5cdd83bce4415932d7c41a86f87d44be2674ff6a01a504aed383b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total **books** (n₁ + n₂) = 52 + 47 = 99

⇒ Total **cost** from Shop 1 = 52 × 1130 = 58760

⇒ Total **cost** from Shop 2 = 47 × 900 = 42300

⇒ Combined Total Cost = 58760 + 42300 = 101060

⇒ Average Price per book = 101060 ÷ 99

⇒ Average Price = 1020.80808... ≈ 1020.81

**∴ The correct answer is 1020.81.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

It is the average where each quantity is assigned a specific weight. Formula: A = (Σ wᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σ wᵢ.

Deviation Method

This method calculates the average by measuring how much each value differs from an assumed mean. It simplifies calculations with large numbers.

Net Change in Average

When elements are added or removed, New Average = (Old Total ± New Values) ÷ (Old Count ± New Count).</p

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 16. If one of the numbers is excluded, the average becomes 17. Find the excluded number.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

Average Concept

Average is defined as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = Σx / n.

When one value is excluded, the excluded value = (Old Average × Old Number of items) − (New Average × New Number of items).

If the excluded number is **greater** than the original average, the average decreases. If it is **smaller**, the average increases.</p

questions.question: A batsman scored 84 runs in his 12th innings, thereby improving his average score per innings by 4 runs. What is the average score per innings of the batsman after the 12th innings?

questions.question: The average of 38 numbers is 51. The average of the first 24 numbers is 45, and that of the last 5 numbers is 60. What is the average of the remaining numbers?

Net deviation from **overall average** 51:

**Required average** = 51 + 11 = 62

**∴ The correct answer is 62.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ **Sum of remaining 9 numbers** = 1938 − 1380 = 558

⇒ **Average of remaining numbers** = 558 ÷ 9 = 62

**∴ The correct answer is 62.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Change in Average

questions.question:
The average of the results of 35 tests is 21. The average of the first 17 results is 19 and the average of the last 17 is 22. What is the value of the result of the 18th test?

A. 42

B. 36

C. 38

D. 34
questions.solution:
The average of the results of 35 tests = 21

The average of the first 17 results = 19

The average of the last 17 results = 22. 

**Concept used:**

Average = sum of elements/number of elements

**Calculation:**

Sum of 35 tests = 21 × 35 

Sum of first 17 tests = 19 × 17 

Sum of last 17 tests = 22 × 17 

Sum of 35 tests = Sum of first 17 tests + 18 th test + Sum of last 17 tests

21 × 35 = 17 × 19 + 17 × 22 + 18 th test

18 test = 21 × 35 - 17 × 41 = 38 

**∴ The result of the 18 th test is 38.**

questions.question: Team India scored runs in the first 30 overs in an ODI match at an average of 5.6 runs per over. What is the required runs per over in the remaining 20 overs at which the team has to score to meet a total target of 320?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Run rate (R1) for first 30 overs = 5.6 runs per over

Total target (T) = 320 runs

Total number of overs = 50

**FORMULA USED:**

Total runs = Run rate × no. of overs

**Calculations:**

For first 30 overs,

Total runs (T1) = R1 x no. of overs

⇒ 5.6 × 30 = 168 runs

For next 20 overs,

Total runs (T2) = T - T1

⇒ 320 - 168 = 152 runs

Now Run rate (R2) = T2 / no. of overs 

⇒ 152 / 20 = 7.6 run
s per over.

**∴ Team India needs run rate of 7.6 runs per over to achieve the target of 320 runs.**
